target_customer: Software and security teams that want automated vulnerability finding and patching in their codebases
problem: Manual security audits are slow and static scanners produce many false positives. winfunc runs an AI agent that finds, verifies in a sandbox and patches vulnerabilities.
business_model: B2B SaaS security tooling (pricing not found)
product_category: AI security engineering and code auditing

founders.name: Mufeed VH
previous_startups: Devika, an open source AI software engineer project (not stated as a company)
founders.background_notes: Per the launch post cited on the YC page, he represented India at the WorldSkills CTF and won medals at national and BRICS skills CTFs.

founders.name: Vivek R
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as CTO at Asterisk, the company's earlier name, with distributed systems, IoT and consulting experience.

technical_complexity.rationale: Autonomous agents that discover business logic bugs and verify exploits in a sandbox with few false positives were hard in mid 2024, when model reasoning was still limited.

defensibility.rationale: Verification in a sandbox and vulnerability research track record help, but frontier model vendors and several funded AI pentest startups were expected to compete on the same capability.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent move against or acquisition of winfunc was found. Other AI pentest startups raised large rounds in 2025 and 2026 per search results, but those are later entrants.

market_need_then: Security audits are costly and slow, and the company reports its agent found vulnerabilities in widely used open source projects. No dated customer or spend data was found.

branding.domain_note: Uses winfunc.com, an exact .com. The earlier name Asterisk used asterisk.so.

identity.visual_style: Developer and research oriented, publishes security research posts
identity.voice_and_tone: Technical and bold, positions the product as an AI hacker

branding.brand_signature: The 'AI Hacker' framing and public vulnerability research posts
branding.community_and_virality: The CEO's open source Devika project is reported to have more than 18,000 GitHub stars, which gave the founder a developer audience.

brand_strength.rationale: Sources show a rebrand from Asterisk and research posts as brand assets, but no press about the brand itself. The founder's Devika following likely helped awareness.

outcome_analysis: winfunc, formerly Asterisk, joined YC in Summer 2024 and is still active with a tiny team. No priced round, acquisition or shutdown was found. The founders have security and open source credibility, but the AI pentest field drew large funding for competitors, and with no disclosed funding the outcome remains unclear.
notes: winfunc.com could not be fetched (HTTP 500 twice), so the company website was not read. Funding: aggregators say about $500K from Y Combinator, which they label an estimate based on the standard YC deal; one aggregator claims $70M, which looks wrong. None are recorded as rounds.
